subject: Options for Dedicated Pool: perf/$ tradeoffs (H100 vs A100 vs L40S) and committed throughput
messages:
From: Susan Tan <susan.tan@optiscale.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Apr 2028 20:21:00 +0000
Subject: Dedicated capacity inquiry — perf/$ and committed throughput

Hi Marissa / Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We ran the sample traces over the weekend and want to start formalizing a dedicated capacity proposal. A few high-level constraints from procurement/infra:
- Target steady-state throughput: ~300 sustained user-concurrent requests at median 1k tokens per response (roughly 300k tokens/min)
- Burst headroom: ability to handle 2x steady-state for short windows (5–10 minutes)
- Preference: H100 for lower tail latency on chat paths, but budget is tight. We want to understand perf/$ (latency tokens per dollar) across H100, A100, L40S and how memory (40/80/96/128GB) changes the economics.

Attached is our workload profile (optiscale_workload_profile.csv) with percentile latency targets. Can Redwood propose 2–3 packaging options (minimal committed commit, mid-tier commit, and a performance-tier) with SLAs and the associated discounts / credit structure? Specifically: how do you price guaranteed throughput vs reserved GPU count, and what levers are available to trade discount for longer terms, stricter SLOs, or a memory-tilt (more 80GB+)?

Also note we operate primarily in us-east-1. Legal will want a clear escalation path and SLO credit formula.

Susan
Head of Infrastructure
OptiScale

Attachments: optiscale_workload_profile.csv
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Susan Tan <susan.tan@optiscale.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Apr 2028 02:06:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity inquiry — perf/$ and committed throughput

Hi Susan — appreciate the profile and the clear constraints. High level we can offer three distinct packaging families (summary below); I'll attach a pricing workbook with SKU-level perf/$ and a simple cost model so you can tweak token/sec assumptions.

1) Efficiency band (cost-first)
- GPU mix: L40S-heavy (L40S for most baseline inference), optional small A100 set for large-batch/embeddings
- Throughput guarantee: soft SLO (90th pct window) with burst crediting; best perf/$ for batch-heavy workloads
- Commit: 12-month reserved commit or 6-mo rolling with higher rates
- Typical discount: ~25–35% vs on-demand depending on commitment length

2) Balanced band (latency-sensitive)
- GPU mix: A100 80GB + L40S as a cost/latency blend
- Throughput guarantee: 95th pct latency SLO, burst allowance for short windows (2x for 10 min)
- Commit: 12–24 month; larger discounts when committed throughput (tokens/min) locked
- Typical discount: ~35–45%

3) Performance band (tail/latency-first)
- GPU mix: H100 80/94GB primary, optional 80GB A100 fallbacks for preemptive scaling
- Throughput guarantee: 99th pct tail SLO with explicit token/sec SLA and financial credits for breaches
- Commit: 24-month preferred; supports hard throughput reservations (we provision dedicated pool to meet throughputs within region)
- Typical discount: 40–55% plus potential service credits for long-term purchase commitments

Pricing levers and notes:
- Memory tilt: moving from 40 -> 80GB reduces the need for cross-shard KV fetches and lowers end-to-end latency; we model this as a 10–25% effective perf uplift depending on your model family (Llama-derivative vs dense decoder). The workbook includes perf/$ curves per GPU type + memory tier.
- Burst capacity: available as a paid add-on (consumable credits) or as reserved burst headroom (part of a higher-tier commit). Reserved burst gives stronger guarantees at higher commit tiers.
- SLA credits: computed monthly as (SLO_target - observed)/SLO_target * committed_monthly_fee * credit_factor. We can provide the exact formula for legal.

I've attached Redwood_Dedicated_Pricing_v1.xlsx and SKU_breakdown.csv with perf tests (99/95/50 pct) using your sample traces scaled to target tokens/min. Would you like a quick 30-minute call Thursday to walk through the workbook and a blended perf/$ scenario with a heavy H100 tilt?

Best,
Marissa
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_Dedicated_Pricing_v1.xlsx, SKU_breakdown.csv
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Apr 2028 09:42:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity inquiry — internal notes

Looping in a couple of negotiation points for the call:
- Offer a blended-deal: price H100 at a premium for up to 60% of steady-state throughput, and cap the rest on L40S. That preserves perf while keeping cost visible.
- Add a 6-month step-down schedule for committed tokens/min if they want optional business flexibility (e.g., month 7–12 rate +15% if they step down).
- Include a 10% one-time onboarding credit for early migration/benchmarking (helps close).
- For legal: pre-define the measurement windows (5-min rolling for burst, 1-hr for SLO lookback) and a conservative warm-up allowance for cache/KV priming.

I'll be on the call and can walk the perf/$ curves in the workbook.

—Karthik
Head of Dedicated Products
Redwood Inference
From: Susan Tan <susan.tan@optiscale.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Apr 2028 15:10:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity inquiry — follow-ups

Thanks Marissa/Karthik. A few clarifying asks before the call:
1) Can you include numeric perf/$ examples (tokens/sec per $1k) for: H100 80GB, A100 80GB, and L40S 40GB using our workload (attached). We need a 3-line comparison for procurement to present.
2) On the blended-deal: we prefer H100 for steady-state latency; we can accept 50% of steady-state on L40S if that materially improves cost. Can you show us a blended example (50% H100 50% L40S) vs 100% H100 for both 12- and 24-month commits with discounts and a burst pricing add-on?
3) On the SLA credits: we need explicit worst-case monthly credit caps (e.g., not to exceed 50% of monthly fee) and a maximum aggregate credit per 12mo.

If you can attach a short one-pager with the numbers, procurement will be happy. We aim to finalize vendor selection by May 2.

Susan

Susan — thanks for the clarity. Attached is a concise one-pager plus an updated proposal (optiscale_proposal_redwood_v2.pdf) and model outputs:
- Numeric perf/$ (tokens/sec per $1k) for your traces: H100(80GB): ~1.9M tokens/sec per $1k; A100(80GB): ~1.2M tokens/sec per $1k; L40S(40GB): ~0.85M tokens/sec per $1k (these are baseline numbers before KV/prefix caching effects).
- Blended example (50% H100 / 50% L40S) for steady-state 300k tokens/min:
  * 12-mo commit: blended effective discount 37%, est monthly spend $xyzk (see PDF), burst add-on priced as a pool of 2x credits for 10 min = $6k/month
  * 24-mo commit: blended effective discount 47%, est monthly spend $xyzk, burst included at higher commit tiers at no additional per-month fee (up to 2x for 10 min)
- SLA credit caps: we propose worst-case monthly credit cap = 40% of monthly fee; aggregate 12mo cap = 120% of 1 month fee (we are willing to discuss adjusting to your legal target of 50%/150%).

Negotiation levers we highlighted for procurement: term length, memory tilt (moving more 80GB H100 lowers tail latency and reduces token consumption), and onboarding credits. We also included a stepped reduction schedule (month 13–24) in the PDF if you need partial flexibility.

If this looks good, I'll ask Solutions Engineering to schedule an on-site benchmark (cost covered by Redwood with a 1-time onboarding credit applied) and route a draft term sheet to legal. Proposed deal id DI-78291.

Best,
Marissa
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
